items.title: Sylvester Handy Interview, 1961-12-13
items.q: And I worked with Papa Celestan.

ctx.x: Did you have the San Jacinto then?

The San Jacinto. We worked from Rhapsody to San Jacinto. And we had nice engagements from jobs to jobs, you know. And there for a while. Beansie still would take out the money for his violin until it was paid for. Well, after it was paid for, they had another fella by the name of Jerry Green. And Jerry Green, he joined the band, which was a bass player, and he'd taken the violin over. And he worked with them for years and years and years. After then, the band broke up for some cause. And then the violin come back…
You heard it back? No, you can hear it. I don't know. I've heard of it. You heard of it.

items.title: Crescent City Crystals: Dave Bailey, Harold Christophe, Albert Delone, Sylvester Handy Interview, 1963-11-13
items.q: I played with, uh, uh, Celestan.

ctx.x: Born in New Orleans and the Trimmy.

Trimmy? Oh, I know. From Trimmy to the Rocky Green. Like London Avenue. 7-Watt, you know? What... Who taught you to play guitar? Now, who taught me how to play guitar? My father played guitar, you see? Yeah. But my first instrument, I used to pick up his guitar. Uh-huh. And all that harmony was right in my head. Yeah. Sure, I guess from listening to him, you pick up... Yeah, and definitely I would get beaten for fooling the guitar. Yeah. You know what I mean? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. But then I started out on the…
